title: Browser subprocess isolation and resource tracking invariant
answers: How does the Browser addon configure proxy routing and profile isolation?
Why must browser launchers register temporary directories and subprocesses?
What flags are required when launching Chromium-based browsers in mitmproxy?
body:
Browser launchers in mitmproxy/addons/browser.py:Browser must configure an isolated session with --user-data-dir and proxy routing via --proxy-server using ctx.options.listen_host and listen_port.
Every browser launch must allocate a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory appended to self.tdir and append the spawned subprocess.Popen instance to self.browser.
Enforced in mitmproxy/addons/browser.py:Browser.launch_edge and Browser.launch_chrome.
Failing to configure flags or track these resources leads to traffic bypassing mitmproxy and leaked temporary profile directories or orphaned processes.
says: Launched browser sessions are leaking temporary profile folders and leaving background processes running.
Traffic from the spawned browser bypasses the proxy because routing flags were missed.
Closing the proxy leaves orphaned browser windows and temporary directories on disk.
Ensure launched browser instances always use a clean profile routed through the proxy.
